items.body_excerpt:
**Anglicanism**, also known as **Episcopalianism** in some countries,[^6] [^7] is a [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Christianity "Western Christianity") [Christian tradition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_tradition "Christian tradition") which developed from the practices, [liturgy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_liturgy "Christian liturgy") and identity of the [Church of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_England "Church of England") following the [English Reformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Reformation "English Reformation"),[^8] in the context of the [Protestant Reformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Reformation "Protestant Reformation") in Europe. It is one of the largest branches of [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"), with around 110 million adherents within the [Anglican Communion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Communion "Anglican Communion"), and approximately 2.4 million outside of the Anglican Communion, worldwide as of 2025.[^9] [^10] [^11] [^12] [^13]

Adherents of Anglicanism are called *Anglicans*; they are also called *Episcopalians* [^14] in some countries. Most are members of national or regional [ecclesiastical provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecclesiastical_province#Anglican_Communion "Ecclesiastical province") of the international Anglican Communion,[^15] one of the largest Christian bodies in the world,[^16] and the world's third-largest Christian communion.[^9] [^17] [^18] [^19] [^20] [^21] The provinces within the Anglican Communion have historically been in [full communion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_communion "Full communion") with the [See of Canterbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/See_of_Canterbury "See of Canterbury") and thus with the [archbishop of Canterbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbishop_of_Canterbury "Archbishop of Canterbury"), whom the communion refers to as its *[primus inter pares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primus_inter_pares#Anglican_Communion "Primus inter pares")* ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin"), 'first among equals'). The archbishop calls the decennial [Lambeth Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambeth_Conference "Lambeth Conference"), chairs the meeting of [primates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primates_in_the_Anglican_Communion "Primates in the Anglican Communion"), and is the president of the [Anglican Consultative Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Consultative_Council "Anglican Consultative Council").[^22] [^23] Some churches that are not part of the Anglican Communion or recognised by it also call themselves Anglican, including those that are within the [Continuing Anglican movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuing_Anglican_movement "Continuing Anglican movement") and [Anglican realignment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_realignment "Anglican realignment").[^24]

Anglicans base their Christian faith on the [Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant_Bible "Protestant Bible"), traditions of the apostolic church, [apostolic succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_succession "Apostolic succession") (" [historic episcopate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historic_episcopate_\(Anglican_views\) "Historic episcopate (Anglican views)") "), and the writings of the [Church Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_Fathers "Church Fathers"), as well as, historically, the *[Thirty-nine Articles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty-nine_Articles "Thirty-nine Articles")* and *[The Books of Homilies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Books_of_Homilies "The Books of Homilies")*.[^25] [^8]

Anglicanism forms a branch of [Western Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Christianity "Western Christianity"), having declared its independence from the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") through the [Act of Supremacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acts_of_Supremacy "Acts of Supremacy") in 1534, a separation later consolidated by the [Elizabethan Religious Settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabethan_Religious_Settlement "Elizabethan Religious Settlement"). Many of the Anglican formularies of the mid-16th century correspond closely to those of historical [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism").[^26] In the first half of the 17th century, the Church of England and the associated [Church of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Ireland "Church of Ireland") were presented by some Anglican divines as comprising a distinct Christian tradition, with theologies, structures, and forms of worship representing a different kind of middle way, or *[via media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_media "Via media")*, originally between Lutheranism and Calvinism,[^27] [^28] and later between Protestantism and Catholicism – a perspective that came to be highly influential in later theories of Anglican identity and expressed in the description of Anglicanism as "catholic and reformed".[^29] The degree of distinction between Protestant and Catholic tendencies within Anglicanism is routinely a matter of debate both within specific Anglican churches and the Anglican Communion. The *[Book of Common Prayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Common_Prayer "Book of Common Prayer")* is unique to Anglicanism, the collection of services in one prayer book used for centuries. The book is acknowledged as a principal tie that binds the Anglican Communion as a liturgical tradition.[^25]

After the [American Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution "American Revolution"), Anglican congregations in the United States and [British North America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_North_America "British North America") (which would later form the basis for the modern country of Canada) were each reconstituted into autonomous churches with their own bishops and self-governing structures; these were known as the [Protestant Episcopal Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_Church_\(United_States\) "Episcopal Church (United States)") in the United States and the [Church of England in the Dominion of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Church_of_Canada "Anglican Church of Canada"). Through the expansion of the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") and the activity of [Christian missions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_mission "Christian mission"), this model was adopted as the model for many newly formed churches, especially in Africa, [Australasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasia "Australasia"), and the Asia-Pacific. In the late-19th century, the term *Anglicanism* was coined to describe the common religious tradition of these churches and also that of the [Scottish Episcopal Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Episcopal_Church "Scottish Episcopal Church"), which, though originating earlier within the [Church of Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Scotland "Church of Scotland"), had come to be recognised as sharing this common identity. By the 21st century, the global centre of Anglicanism had shifted to the [Global South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_South "Global South"), particularly sub-Saharan Africa, with 63,556,000 in Africa, 24,400,000 in Europe, 4,565,000 in Oceania, 2,689,000 in Northern America, 1,230,000 in Asia, and 959,000 in Latin America in 2020.[^30] [^31]

## A Simple Mission

Dr. John Matthias has a simple mission – to facilitate self-discovery to make a difference in the world, whether this involves helping clients to overcome past traumas or to become exceptional leaders or parents. He has primarily worked as a [clinical psychologist](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534/http://www.apa.org/ed/graduate/specialize/clinical.aspx) and as an organizational consultant with a focus upon leadership for several major organizations, including the [Andre Agassi Foundation](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534/http://www.agassifoundation.org/). He has been fortunate to have had several exceptional mentors, including the pioneering psychologist Rodney Goodyear and the leadership guru [Warren Bennis](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534/http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Bennis) while receiving his doctorate from the University of Southern California. Dr. Matthias also graduated with honors in philosophy from Princeton University under the guidance of the renowned philosopher, [Gilbert Harman](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534/http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Harman). He won the prestigious McCosh Thesis prize at Princeton University. He was an All-Chicago and All-State football player in high school and he played college football at Princeton. He was also high school valedictorian at a large public high school in Chicago where he was chosen for a valedictory study that continues to this day.

![https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/BanksFeminist.jpg](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/BanksFeminist.jpg "SHA-256: 1a1f48113891928b14a6b18a908b2987fbb618c792871d5aac1ab072addf4885")

Dr. Matthias has acquired an enormous depth and breath of psychological knowledge over his twenty year career as a psychologist, including in the domains of forensic, clinical, family and [organizational psychology](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534/http://www.apa.org/ed/graduate/specialize/industrial.aspx). In the forensic context he has assessed hundreds of high risk felons for community placement, developing expertise in personality assessments and hidden behavioral motivations. In the clinical realm he has worked with numerous victims of abuse and trauma, including with survivors of the recent Las Vegas shooting massacre and 9/11. As a family therapist Dr. Matthias received his Master’s degree in Marriage, Family and Child counseling and he has worked with hundreds of families, couples and children over the years. He still supervises UNLV doctoral students on play therapy and family systems. As an organizational consultant he has worked with many community leaders and CEO’s, assisting them to achieve insight and excellence in their domains. He has also worked with several organizations seeking transformation by applying a unique research model he developed drawing parallels between the qualities of exceptional teams and exceptional families. By working with individuals and groups across such a wide spectrum of areas that have included both deficits and strengths, Dr. Matthias has developed a keen understanding of human beings at their highest and lowest points across the entire spectrum of human psychological development and functioning, which has led to greater wisdom about the major ingredients necessary for mastery and the development of resiliency and psychological well-being.

## Challenged by Warren Bennis

to develop a grand unified theory of leadership many years ago, Dr. Matthias has become increasingly interested in the impact of exceptional leadership and the ability of strong leaders to leave a mark on the world. He has also explored the elements of mastery across many domains, including therapy and personality assessment. Toward that end, he has trained numerous doctoral students in clinical psychology at UNLV- many of whom have gone onto leadership positions in their organizations. He has also worked with leaders in many domains, including sports, health care, and business, to assist them in broadening their influence and he has helped many individuals on their paths towards mastery. He has been guided by the persistent questions: What makes an exceptional leader? And are there any common elements for leadership and mastery across domains? He is currently writing two books addressing these questions. The first book, *Strive: The New Psychology of Meaning and Mastery*, will be published in 2019. The second book, *Leading Lives: Wednesdays with Warren Bennis and the Search for a Grand Unified Theory of Leadership*, will be published in 2020. He also recently started a podcast- Strive- to assist people in striving for meaning and mastery through conversations with remarkable people and academics who share their ideas, research and stories about their personal journeys to strive for meaning and mastery in their daily lives and work with the goal of helping others to do the same.

![https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Banks-at-SnowCanyon.jpg](https://web.archive.org/web/20180817210534im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Banks-at-SnowCanyon.jpg "SHA-256: 09c9b63c95cd81acdf32c0f62575617ed3ab00dda0cd1493ab7975d932343d9d")

## PROJECTS iHOPE & iSTRIVE

Dr. Matthias recently launched two initiatives- Project iHope, which provides adventure experiences for children with terminal illnesses and their families, and Project iStrive, which provides a platform for individuals to share their most passionate strivings for the future.

Dr. Matthias is a licensed psychologist in both Utah and Nevada. He is an adjunct faculty member at the University of Nevada Las Vegas in the clinical psychology doctoral program. He is also a certified Eagala mental health specialist and he often incorporates equine work into his adventure experiences. He is an avid canyoneer and he gains sustenance and energy from the beautiful canyons of Southern Utah. As a new father of a beautiful baby boy, Dr. John holds out hope for a future worth inhabiting. His personal mission is to strive for love, peace, wisdom, kindness, knowledge and service to others.

You can learn more about Dr. Matthias from his abbreviated autobiographical blog post, **In Praise of All Things Wild**.

A Short Autobiography

[![https://web.archive.org/web/20180816073155im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Wild-Things-Parade.jpg](https://web.archive.org/web/20180816073155im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Wild-Things-Parade.jpg "SHA-…
items.body_excerpt:
A Short Autobiography

[![https://web.archive.org/web/20180816073155im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Wild-Things-Parade.jpg](https://web.archive.org/web/20180816073155im_/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Wild-Things-Parade.jpg "SHA-256: bb61b1323e7c76b2ac9c362fda1c3b04faa8f234217dd9f5a4b6e4cdee5936f9")](https://web.archive.org/web/20180816073155/http://strivepsychology.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Wild-Things-Parade.jpg)

When I was five years old my mother accelerated onto the on ramp of Willow Road outside of Chicago and the side door, which had been slightly ajar, inadvertently swung open, tossing my unsuspecting body out onto the highway like someone losing control of an empty brown McDonald’s bag sitting in the back seat of the car for days and waiting to be thrown out.

Instinctively, I rolled onto the pavement at 40 miles per hour and tucked into the fetal position when I spied a semi-truck approaching from behind. My outstretched arms hit the pavement, tearing the skin open and leaving a two-foot long trail of blood painted along the white lines of the highway. When I curled my knees into my body the pool of blood soaked into my t-shirt. The truck swerved slightly, trying to avoid me, but the driver realized the futility of such a last-minute adjustment and he swung the truck directly over my now motionless body. Drips of corrosive diesel engulfed my body, the engine wailed and hummed as the brakes screeched in a last ditch effort to right the truck, the muffler grazed my shoulder, shredding my t-shirt and skin, and the semi-truck thrust me out of its entrails without much fanfare.

When the driver pulled over the to side of the road everyone, including my mother, assumed I was dead. Ongoing traffic swerved to avoid my motionless body, still tucked in the middle of one of the busiest highways in suburban Chicago, until I gathered myself, stood up and ran across the road to safety. From across the four-lane divide I could see my mother crying. It was the first and last time I have ever witnessed my mother crying. The truck driver told my mother that he had heard a loud thud sound as his truck careened over my body and he knew I had been instantly killed. It was the muffler swiping my shoulder. The truck driver had been crying too. My body’s brief immobility in the middle of the road only added to the worries.

My mother asked me if I was hurt. I said no. Even then I was learning the value of being stoic. We drove home without any discussion of the incident. My mother never told my father about the accident and there was no visit to the hospital, even though my body hurt for months afterwards. Blood soaked my t-shirt and blue jeans.

From that moment forward the accident was relegated to complete silence for nearly forty years, as if it only existed in some imaginary world that children inhabit, as if the entire incident had merely been a looney-toons cartoon and I was the roadrunner who got up unscathed from under the anvil every time.

Except I wasn’t unscathed. My body had healed, but the emotional wounds from the accident cut an invisibly cavernous swath within my small five-year-old body that ran deep and wide, touching every capillary and blood vessel running into and out of my heart and every nerve ending and axon seeking entrance and exit from my brain.

The nightmares began suddenly and without warning on the evening of the accident. A semi-truck rolling down the freeway, out of control, swerving frantically, plowing directly into my body. On perpetual repeat, over and over. I awaken twenty times on that first night. Every time my head hits the pillow I meet that same semi-truck again and again, rolling on down the road and heading in only one direction. Each morning I awake without rest, my pillow and sheets drenched in sweat. I begin to turn on my bedroom light each night to make the nightmares subside. They continue, unabated. Same truck, same story, same result. On repeat, over and over. Eventually the semi-truck evolves into a train and then the train becomes an airplane. The objects become larger and more foreboding with each passing week, each one rolling head on directly into my child’s body and fragile psyche. The ingenuity of the imagination is limitless, especially if survival depends upon it. As my small head lays down the terror goes up. There are many sleepless nights, many nights when I awake screaming from night terrors. Each dream has the same underlying theme- destruction, violence, death.

Slowly, over time, these objects of death begin to transform. The trucks become wild predators, the trains become amorphous monsters, the planes become vampires. Monsters- those objects of social disruption and mayhem, those objects displacing the status quo, those objects assaulting our safety and complacency- begin to creep into my dreams until they become an obsession. I’m watching monster movies whenever I can, even though I’m much too young to understand them. My mother allows it because she experiences such guilt. My other two siblings sleep soundly in bed as I burn the midnight oil in front of horror movies. I build models of monsters. I clip pictures of the most frightening images I can find, keeping them in a spiral notebook, as if somehow classifying and binding them can keep them at bay. It doesn’t work, it’s too late. The creatures have been loosed upon my imagination.

I now understand that these monsters symbolized death, plain and simple, staking a massive claim on my naively impressionistic mind. No child should have to face the constant threat of death every day, whether real or imaginary. I had joined admittance into an unenviable club of children facing terminal illnesses, war, cancer, and severe abuse, although no one understood the magnitude of my symptoms at the time. Today I would have been diagnosed with childhood posttraumatic stress disorder. My symptoms were classic- constant flashbacks, nightmares, depression, anger, isolation, fear and insomnia. On most days the PTSD club door remained locked and there was no way out except to venture into my turbulent dreams, which greeted me with the slight relief of engaging the monsters head on. At least in my dreams I could confront my enemies head on, even as I lost every battle I ever fought. During the day my flashbacks were incessant, bombarding me with a frequency and intensity that would be hard to describe. I remember one day in first grade when my body was so soaked with sweat that the teacher believed I had just fallen into a pond. She asked me if I had somehow during recess taken a swim in a nearby pond. I said no. I had stayed inside the entire time. The constant sweats became an uncontrollable anxiety now pervading every night and day of my young existence. By age 6 I had lost control of my body to an unrelenting anxiety, my mind refused to focus on thoughts other than traumatic ones and my shame from these perverse concessions was becoming unbearable. I fell into a dark childhood depression.

My response to these circumstances was isolation and spending increasingly large amounts of time in nature. A small tributary of the Chicago river ran behind our home and I spent most of my free time either in or on the river, trying desperately to fathom its secrets. Perhaps a glimpse into the mysteries of the river might assuage my pain, if only momentarily. If the heart is a lonely hunter then I had been marooned on an island in the middle of the Chicago river, unable to swim to shore even with my home in sight. I was lonely beyond compare, trapped in a body and mind that only knew despair and pain. At 6 years old I saw no way out. My mother always watched me from afar, aware of my suffering and isolation, aware of our secret. She felt powerless to intervene and afraid to broach a taboo topic.

items.title: ## The Richard Allen Trial: "Evidence", Flaws, and Wrongful Conviction
items.summary:
## The Richard Allen Trial: "Evidence", Flaws, and Wrongful Conviction

---

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015769007-3.jpg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015769007-3.jpg "SHA-256: 1098d73019b4442e423313ef86c39efc87a1c21742708e809e…
items.body_excerpt:
## The Richard Allen Trial: "Evidence", Flaws, and Wrongful Conviction

---

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015769007-3.jpg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015769007-3.jpg "SHA-256: 1098d73019b4442e423313ef86c39efc87a1c21742708e809ea92812d5aa639d")

Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka

The trial of Richard Allen for the 2017 Delphi murders of Abigail Williams and Liberty German resulted in his conviction and a 130-year sentence. However, significant flaws in the prosecution’s case, combined with a lack of definitive evidence, raise serious questions about the integrity of the verdict. These pages provide a detailed, point-by-point breakdown of the trial, organized into relevant subsections, analyzing the prosecution’s arguments, the defense case, and overarching issues that suggest a potential wrongful conviction.

On February 13, 2017, Abigail "Abby" Williams (13) and Liberty "Libby" German (14) were murdered near the Monon High Bridge trail in Delphi, Indiana. The case remained unsolved for years, gaining national and international attention due to a grainy video and audio clip from Libby’s phone capturing a man saying, “Guys, down the hill.” In 2022, Richard Allen, a local resident, was arrested and charged with the murders. The prosecution’s case relied heavily on alleged confessions, a contested ballistic match, and circumstantial evidence placing Allen at the scene. The defense argued that Allen was wrongfully convicted based on coerced statements, unreliable evidence, and investigative failures.

---

### Breaking Down the Case for Innocence

The trial of Richard Allen - as well as the seven-year machinations surrounding the murders more broadly - is unwieldy and at time difficult to see through. We've broken down the case for innocence into three main areas to help you quickly understand the evidential, judicial, and third-party suspect concerns:

1. [Read about the nine primary pieces of evidence used at trial »](#evidence)
2. [Read about the questionable conduct of Special Judge Frances Gull »](https://rickallenjustice.com/judge-gulls-role-a-question-of-judicial-fairness/)
3. [Learn about the Franks Memo, which outlines plausible third-party suspects »](https://rickallenjustice.com/the-franks-memo-explained/)
4. [Read about the leading studies on false confessions »](https://rickallenjustice.com/false-confessions-undermine-justice/)

---

### The Questionable Evidence Used to Convict Richard Allen

Below, we summarize the nine primary pieces of evidence presented by the state and the defense’s counterarguments. Click through to each of these for further information, and assess for yourself if the state reached the *beyond reasonable doubt* watermark.

**A. Richard Allen’s Alleged Confessions** 
Allen’s so-called confessions were coerced under harsh solitary confinement, raising serious doubts about their reliability. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/richard-allens-alleged-confessions/) 
 
**B. The Unspent Bullet** 
The prosecution’s key bullet evidence was contested, with no independent verification to confirm its link to Allen’s gun. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/the-unspent-bullet/) 
 
**C. Allen’s Presence and Timeline at the Trails** 
Vague witness accounts failed to definitively place Allen at the crime scene during the murders. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/allens-presence-and-timeline-at-the-trails/) 
 
**D. The “Van Detail” Confession** 
Allen’s mention of a van, claimed as "killer-only knowledge", was widely known and lacked exclusivity. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/the-van-detail-confession/) 
 
**E. Sarah Carbaugh’s Testimony** 
Sarah Carbaugh’s inconsistent account of a man on the highway was too unreliable to incriminate Allen. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/sarah-carbaughs-testimony/) 
 
**F. Allen’s Vehicle Identification** 
The late identification of Allen’s car was criticized as a desperate attempt to fit evidence to the suspect. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/allens-vehicle-identification/) 
 
**G. Voice Identification on Libby’s Phone** 
Subjective voice identification by an involved officer lacked the forensic rigor needed to tie Allen to the crime. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/voice-identification-on-libbys-phone/) 
 
**H. Dr. Kohr’s Autopsy Findings** 
Dr. Kohr’s revised weapon theory, prompted by prosecutors, cast doubt on the autopsy’s impartiality. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/dr-kohrs-autopsy-findings/) 
 
**I. Libby’s Phone Data** 
Unexplained activity on Libby’s phone long after the murders suggests possible evidence tampering. 
[Learn more »](https://rickallenjustice.com/libbys-phone-data/)

---

### Verdict and Sentencing

On November 11, 2024, after 19 hours of deliberation, a jury from Allen County - brought in to Carroll County for the trial - found Richard Allen guilty on all four counts: two counts of murder, and two counts of felony murder while committing or attempting to commit kidnapping. The verdict came after 17 days of testimony in a trial marked by intense public scrutiny and emotional weight, as evidenced by the crowd’s mixed reactions outside the courtroom, with some cheering the outcome and others holding signs supporting Allen’s innocence.

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015768007-1.jpg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015768007-1.jpg "SHA-256: c2eb128b39cc230c515c44c33b63cc7db505e66aacfb773ce26f749ba109f58d")

Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka

**Sentencing: December 20, 2024** 
On December 20, 2024, Judge Gull sentenced Allen to the maximum of 130 years in prison, imposing 65 years for each of two murder counts to be served consecutively. The sentencing hearing, lasting under two hours, included six victim impact statements from the victims’ relatives, underscoring the profound loss felt by their families. However, the defense, led by attorney Jennifer Auger, immediately announced plans to appeal and seek a new trial, signaling their belief that justice was not served. The maximum sentence is a punishment for a crime *not proven beyond reasonable doubt*, compounding the tragedy of a conviction built on flawed evidence.

---

### Overarching Defense Arguments

**Complete Absence of Forensic Evidence** 
The defense repeatedly emphasized that no DNA, fingerprints, footprints, clothing fibers, or trace evidence (e.g., soil, blood) linked Allen to the crime scene, nor was any crime scene evidence found on Allen, his home, or his vehicle. This absence is extraordinary given the violent nature of the crime and the extensive investigation, casting significant doubt on Allen’s guilt.

**Botched Investigation and Tunnel Vision** 
The defense implied investigative failures, such as police failing to retrieve exculpatory evidence (a “mimicked crime scene” photo relating to a third-party suspect) from Georgia themselves and failing to explore alternative theories like the “Odinist” angle referenced in the Franks Memo. These suggest a focus on Allen to the exclusion of other leads, potentially overlooking the true perpetrator.

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015770007-2.jpg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/76015770007-2.jpg "SHA-256: 20be7a4d6ad057698330289ee9b67bf484df95411ee198c105c5bf9ce80bff1f")

The long arm of the law: ISP Superintendent Doug Carter and Prosecutor Nick McLeland ( Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka )

**Allegations of Prosecutorial/Investigative Misconduct** 
The defense raised serious issues about how the case was handled, pointing to possible bias from investigators, including claims that ISP’s Jerry Holeman pushed questionable tactics and misrepresented evidence like the Odinism report. They also criticized Judge Fran Gull for decisions that seemed to favor the prosecution, such as limiting defense arguments, which may have tilted the

items.title: ### "Normal everyday family man"
items.summary: Richard “Rick” Matthew Allen, also known to friends and family as Ricky, spent over 16 years quietly woven into the life of Delphi, Indiana.
items.body_excerpt:
Richard “Rick” Matthew Allen, also known to friends and family as Ricky, spent over 16 years quietly woven into the life of Delphi, Indiana. Before his 2022 arrest and 2024 conviction in the widely publicized Delphi murders case, Rick was known as a friendly face behind the CVS pharmacy counter, a devoted husband and father, and a regular at the local pub. To neighbors and acquaintances, he was “a heck of a nice guy,” someone who “blended in” completely, living a life that, by all outward appearances, was stable, familiar, and unremarkable.

Now serving a 130-year sentence, Allen’s story has become a lightning rod, with many raising serious concerns about the integrity of the trial and the possibility of wrongful conviction. But before all of that, Rick Allen was just Rick: a quiet man in a quiet town.

---

### "Normal everyday family man"

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/IMG_4019.png.jpeg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/IMG_4019.png.jpeg "SHA-256: 8dc113d984498518fd3bd9d8b4dc7a1d4581a3ffeb55db31fa7f0f87b78a9a7c")

Richard Allen at trial, November 2024 (Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka)

Born in September 1972 in Mexico, Indiana, Rick grew up in a small rural community that instilled values of humility, hard work, and routine. He attended North Miami Middle/High School in nearby Denver, where he played football and ran track and field, activities that reflected his enjoyment of teamwork and discipline. He graduated in 1991 and went on to study accounting at Ivy Tech Community College, a practical choice that signaled his intent to build a reliable, structured life.

A former neighbor from those years, David Yoder, described Rick as “an all-around good, normal everyday family man.” Nothing about his early life stood out, except, perhaps, how typical it all seemed.

---

### Marriage, Military, and Management

Shortly after high school, Rick married Kathy on November 19, 1991. The couple welcomed their daughter, Brittany, in 1994, and together they navigated the familiar milestones of early adult life, raising a family, maintaining steady employment, and planting roots in Indiana towns both small and smaller.

At the same time, Rick was serving his country. According to military records, Sergeant Richard Matthew Allen served in the Indiana National Guard from December 5, 1989, to December 4, 1998, a nearly decade-long tenure marked by honorable discharge and no disciplinary actions on record.

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/F9YQZUjXEAk_KUD.jpeg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/F9YQZUjXEAk_KUD.jpeg "SHA-256: fe94ab681f5ef4df071433eecd7f70c6da2569d20fcba41d3a137a13e56e436c")

Richard Allen at trial, November 2024 (Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka)

He was assigned to Alpha Company of the 2nd Battalion 58th Infantry and Charlie Company of the 2nd Battalion 293rd Infantry, the latter of which is now inactive. His roles included Infantryman and Indirect Fire Infantryman.

This service period overlapped with his early years of marriage and fatherhood, suggesting a man balancing civic responsibility with family life. A small but symbolic item - a green and gold Indiana National Guard multi-tool - was later documented among Allen’s personal belongings during his legal proceedings, offering a subtle reminder of his dedication to community.

After completing his time in the Guard, Rick shifted his focus to civilian life. In 2003, he took on a store management role at Walmart in Logansport, Indiana, overseeing a large retail team and daily operations for the next ten years. The job demanded leadership, long hours, and attention to detail, traits he had already honed during his military service. From stocking shelves to handling customer complaints to managing personnel, Rick helped keep the store - and his life - running smoothly until 2013, when he pivoted toward a new chapter.

---

### "A Good Family Couple"

In December 2006, the Allens relocated to Delphi, a small Carroll County town with a population just shy of 3,000. They purchased a modest home near the heart of town, just 2.5 miles from the Monon High Bridge, the future site of an unimaginable tragedy.

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/635c883a27307.image.jpg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/635c883a27307.image.jpg "SHA-256: 167a1999663209b01d0020b122e8581e7d2f585c29473987718cf330baa2453b")

Richard Allen at trial, November 2024 (Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka)

Rick’s life in Delphi was marked by routine and community ties. He and Kathy were known locally as a close couple, often seen together at the Brick & Mortar Pub (formerly JC’s Bar), where they were regulars, visiting several times a week. Conversations often turned to town happenings, including the Delphi murders in 2017. According to Bob Matlock, the bar’s former owner and Rick’s longtime friend, Allen “expressed sympathy for the families” and never raised suspicion. "They were just a good family couple," Matlock recalled.

---

### A Familiar Face at CVS

After leaving Walmart, Rick transitioned into healthcare, taking a job at CVS Pharmacy, first in Peru and later at the Delphi location. In February 2018, he officially became a licensed pharmacy technician, a role requiring discretion, organization, and interpersonal care.

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/0807c096-89c3-4d8d-8224-a55f349a3fd8-jumbo16x9_PRichardAllenDelphiFolo.transfer_frame_608.jpeg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/0807c096-89c3-4d8d-8224-a55f349a3fd8-jumbo16x9_PRichardAllenDelphiFolo.transfer_frame_608.jpeg "SHA-256: f86caf950327bbc89fedecc73bf39327d107a0bd6bad5da4ef1a552bb616b86f")

Richard Allen at trial, November 2024 (Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka)

Rick’s work put him in direct contact with the community, filling prescriptions, helping at the photo counter, and assisting customers. He even processed photos for Libby German’s grandparents, Mike and Becky Patty, and did so without charging them. That act, though seemingly small, is often cited as an example of the kind of man people believed he was: helpful, empathetic, and dependable.

Local residents like Chuck Webb, a CVS regular, described him as friendly and professional. Betty Cummings, another acquaintance, remembered seeing him at McDonald’s, quietly going about his day. "He just blended in," she said.

---

### Snapshots of a Quiet Life

Rick Allen's life in Delphi unfolded in the quiet spaces between work shifts, shared meals, and unremarkable errands, the kind of ordinary, familiar routines that make up most people's lives. He wasn't someone who sought attention. Instead, he moved through his world with a calm presence: polite, dependable, and modest in his habits.

The rhythms of his life were steady. He favored familiar places and familiar people. He had routines, preferences, habits. He played pool. He enjoyed quiet nights out. He laughed easily with friends but didn’t speak loudly. His relationships, especially with those closest to him, were marked by stability and longevity.

![https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/IMG_4017.png.jpeg](https://rickallenjustice.com/content/images/2025/04/IMG_4017.png.jpeg "SHA-256: 2f61561ccc54c5725225ad691dccdc5e1a63738895125710f31059a06cf1f352")

Richard Allen at trial, November 2024 (Courtroom sketches by Li Buszka)

Even in the digital traces left behind - small glimpses of family life shared casually online before the trial - there’s a sense of a life anchored in comfort, privacy, and simplicity. A private moment captured during a road trip, a small joke exchanged with his wife, a family outing on a crisp Indiana day; these are not dramatic or performative, they're snapshots of a simple, family-centered life.

## Richard Allen's Appeal

---

Richard Allen is appealing his convictions and 130-year sentence to the Indiana Court of Appeals.
items.body_excerpt:
## Richard Allen's Appeal

---

Richard Allen is appealing his convictions and 130-year sentence to the Indiana Court of Appeals. This page explains what the appeal is about, where the case stands, and what the Court may decide.

## Current status

**Current as of August 2026:** The written briefing is complete, and oral arguments have been scheduled for **Monday, September 21, 2026, at 10:00 a.m.**

Case

Allen v. State, Indiana Court of Appeals Case No. 25A-CR-00591

Location

Supreme Court Courtroom, State House Room 315, Indianapolis, Indiana

Panel

Judges Nancy H. Vaidik, Elaine B. Brown, and Robert R. Altice, Jr.

Time allowed

Thirty minutes for each side

The scheduling order states that the argument will be webcast at the [Indiana judiciary website](https://www.in.gov/judiciary/) and televised on a monitor outside the courtroom.

## What is this appeal about?

A direct appeal is not a second trial. The Court of Appeals will review the trial record and the legal arguments in the parties' briefs. It will consider whether the trial court made errors that affected the fairness or reliability of the convictions, whether those issues were preserved for review, and what remedy is legally available.

Allen's attorneys argue that the conviction cannot stand because several important decisions shaped what the jury heard and how it understood the evidence. The State argues that many of those claims were waived, that the trial court acted within its discretion, and that any error did not affect the verdict.

This page focuses on the defense case while identifying the State's principal responses. The arguments summarized here are positions taken in the appellate filings, not findings by the Court.

## Appeal timeline

1. **November 11, 2024:** A jury found Allen guilty on all four counts in the Delphi murders case.
2. **December 20, 2024:** The trial court sentenced Allen to 130 years in prison.
3. **March 11, 2025:** Allen's attorneys filed the notice of appeal.
4. **December 17, 2025:** Allen's attorneys filed the opening Appellant's Brief.
5. **March 25, 2026:** The State filed its Appellee's Brief in response.
6. **April 27, 2026:** Allen's attorneys filed the Reply Brief and requested oral argument. The written briefing was then complete.
7. **May 14, 2026:** The Court granted the request for oral argument and set the September hearing.
8. **August 18, 2026:** The Court was informed that copies of three exhibits - HHH, III, and KKK - had been "corrupted". The Court ordered the Court Reporter to file new copies with the Carroll Circuit and Superior Courts Clerk and directed that they be transmitted to the appellate court. This describes what the Court was told and ordered; it is not an independent finding that the exhibits were intentionally altered. [Read why these three exhibits matter »](https://rickallenjustice.com/three-more-exhibits-are-corrupted/)
9. **September 21, 2026:** Oral arguments are scheduled in Indianapolis.

---

## The major issues on appeal

### 1\. The search warrant, the Franks challenge, and the gun evidence

#### What the defense argues

Allen's attorneys argue that the affidavit used to obtain the warrant for his home contained material misstatements and omissions. They point to differences between witness accounts and the way those accounts were presented to the judge who authorized the search, including the description of a man seen near the trail, the description of his clothing, and whether a witness described that man as muddy or bloody.

The defense says the affidavit omitted information that could have weakened probable cause, including an eyewitness description that did not resemble Allen and information about when Allen's jacket was purchased. It argues that the search warrant should be examined under *Franks v. Delaware*, which provides a way to challenge a warrant based on deliberate or reckless falsehoods or omissions.

The defense further argues that the gun and later evidence, including the confessions, flowed from the search. If the warrant was invalid, it says, the Court must consider whether that later evidence should also be excluded.

#### What the State says

The State argues that the issue was waived because Allen did not object to the search evidence at trial. It disputes the claim that the affidavit was false, emphasizing that the witness gave later accounts describing the man as bloody. It also argues that the omitted or challenged information was not material because other evidence supported probable cause and placed Allen on the trail.

#### Why it matters on appeal

The search-warrant issue is important because the gun evidence was obtained during that search. The Court must decide both whether the warrant affidavit was legally adequate and, if not, what evidence the law permits the State to use afterward.

---

### 2\. Solitary confinement, psychosis, and the alleged involuntary confessions

#### What the defense argues

Allen's attorneys argue that the State obtained his statements after a prolonged period of solitary confinement and severe mental deterioration. They point to records describing psychosis, grave disability, antipsychotic medication, and more than a year in restrictive housing. The defense says the conditions were not simply difficult; they were legally relevant to whether Allen could make a rational and voluntary statement.

The defense also argues that investigators used deceptive interrogation techniques before the confinement began, and that many later statements contained factual impossibilities or references to people and events unrelated to the murders. In its view, those statements make more sense as symptoms of a deteriorating mind than as reliable admissions of guilt.

The Reply Brief additionally argues that trial testimony identified no confession before Allen was placed at Westville, challenging the State's attempt to separate statements made before and after the claimed psychosis.

#### What the State says

The State argues that the confession evidence was also waived because the defense did not object to the confession documents at trial. It disputes the causal link between confinement and the statements, pointing to the conditions Allen was provided in his cell and arguing that the confessions began before, continued through, and extended beyond the period of alleged psychosis. The State also offers alternative explanations for the statements, including religious conversion and Allen's access to legal discovery.

#### Why it matters on appeal

The Court must consider whether the trial court applied the correct legal standards to voluntariness and whether the conditions of confinement can make statements inadmissible even when the State does not use physical force during the interview.

---

### 3\. Excluded defense evidence and the right to present a complete defense

#### What the defense argues

Allen's attorneys argue that the trial court prevented the jury from seeing or hearing evidence needed to evaluate the State's case fully. Examples include the composite sketch associated with witness Betsy Blair, expert criticism of the firearms comparison, recordings that would have shown the context of Allen's mental condition, and evidence about activity on Liberty German's phone.

The defense says the jury was allowed to hear the State's interpretation of those subjects while being denied the evidence or expert testimony that would have challenged it. It argues that this created an unfair imbalance and violated the constitutional right to present a complete defense.

It also challenges the admission or use of testimony based on an officer's Google search and internet-forum material to explain phone evidence, arguing that the material was not reliable expert evidence and could not be meaningfully cross-examined.

#### What the State says

The State responds that several of these claims were waived because the evidence was not offered or the objection was not preserv

items.body_excerpt:
On September 13, 2006, 25-year-old Kimveer Singh Gill opened fire at [Dawson College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawson_College "Dawson College"), a [CEGEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEGEP "CEGEP") located in [downtown Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Montreal "Downtown Montreal"), Quebec, Canada. Gill began by shooting outside the [de Maisonneuve Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Maisonneuve_Boulevard "De Maisonneuve Boulevard") entrance to the school, before moving towards the atrium by the cafeteria on the main floor.[^1] [^2] One victim died at the scene, while another 19 were injured, eight of whom were listed in critical condition, with six requiring surgery.[^3] [^4] [^5] The shooter later committed [suicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide "Suicide"), after being shot in the arm by a police officer.[^6] It was the third fatal [school shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_massacre "School massacre") in Montreal, after the [École Polytechnique massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89cole_Polytechnique_massacre "École Polytechnique massacre") in 1989 and the shooting spree at [Concordia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concordia_University_massacre "Concordia University massacre") in 1992.

## Shooting

![https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Dawson-shooting-map.svg/330px-Dawson-shooting-map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Dawson-shooting-map.svg/330px-Dawson-shooting-map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "SHA-256: 1bcb3053b69fb222093ad93a60729f4a282b17d12dafa00042235b0fb8f95104")

1\. 12:30: Shooter exits his car. 2. 12:41: First shots fired outside entrance. 3. 12:44: Nearby officers rush to the scene. 4. 12:42–1:01: Gunman fires on students in the cafeteria. Police shoot him in the arm, he kills himself with a shot to the head. 5. 1:30: Killer's body is dragged outside and covered.

Shortly before 12:40 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Daylight_Time "Eastern Daylight Time"), Gill parked his car on de Maisonneuve Boulevard about 100 metres from the college campus, and was seen removing bags and a [semi-automatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-automatic_rifle "Semi-automatic rifle") [carbine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbine "Carbine") from his trunk by bystanders. One of the bystanders called 911 to report Gill. As Gill walked towards the college, he briefly took a passerby hostage, forcing him to carry a bag containing the [Norinco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norinco "Norinco") shotgun, four knives, a [crowbar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowbar "Crowbar"), and additional ammunition. As Gill and the hostage approached the college, they saw a police vehicle pull over outside the college. Two police officers were visiting the school at the time regarding an unrelated incident about a [drug deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drug_trade "Illegal drug trade").[^7]

Upon seeing the police car, Gill fired 10 shots from his carbine at students outside on the rear entrance steps, emptying the gun. The hostage fled the scene, throwing Gill's bag away.[^8] The first shots were fired at 12:42:01 p.m. Gill injured several students outside the college before jumping over a small wall to enter the school. One of the police officers got out of his vehicle and chased Gill into the college, shouting at him to drop his weapon.[^7]

Gill entered the school at 12:42:12 p.m., making his way to the school cafeteria almost directly ahead of the school entrance. At 12:42:24 p.m., Gill positioned himself in the corner of the building, near a vending machine, setting his bag and carbine on the floor. He loaded a Glock pistol and shot students standing in front of him, wounding several including Anastasia De Sousa. The police officer who chased Gill tried to approach him and leaned against a wall in the cafeteria. Gill reloaded his carbine and fired at the officer. The officer's partner arrived to assist him. After Gill had fired at the officers for several minutes, taunting them, both officers were told by a sergeant to fall back.[^7]

Gill then fired at students crawling to escape the atrium. After wounding students and an employee of the college, Gill took a male student hostage. The hostage lied to Gill about the locations of officers. Gill asked if De Sousa was dead. The hostage said that he didn't know but pleaded with Gill to be allowed to take her outside, promising to come back. Gill asked another student if De Sousa was dead, who also told Gill that he didn't know. Gill fired several more shots into De Sousa from his carbine, yelling, "Now she's dead!" [^7]

Additional police officers arrived at the college. Some entered the floor above the cafeteria while others surrounded the campus.[^9] One of the officers shouted at Gill from the floor above. He exchanged gunfire with Gill, nearly shooting him. The officer fell back and repositioned himself. At one point, Gill aimed his Glock under his chin while announcing that it was his last day. He was interrupted by movement from the floor above and began firing in that direction with his carbine.[^7]

Throughout the standoff, Gill repeatedly peeked out from behind a corner and also tried stepping out before returning.[^7]

At 1:01 p.m., Gill took two students hostage, including the student he had previously taken hostage. He ordered one hostage to retrieve a bag filled with ammunition, then forced the hostages to precede him as he walked north. Officer Denis Côté, who was located on the floor above, fired two quick shots at Gill at 1:01:36 p.m. Gill was struck in the right elbow, the bullet only going through muscle. Gill's carbine was also shot in its stock, which struck Gill in the chest causing a bruise. Gill fell to his knees and placed the Glock in his mouth before shooting himself at 1:01:42 p.m.[^6] [^7] At the same time, Côté fired two more shots, hitting a garbage can.[^7]

The police officers attempted to resuscitate him, but failed. At 1:30 p.m., police officers dragged Gill's body outside, covered it with a yellow bag, then continued the evacuation and the search for possible accomplices.[^10] [^11] Authorities concluded the attack was premeditated, after a short [suicide note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_note "Suicide note") was found on Gill's body during the autopsy.[^12]

The shooter discharged his rifle 72 times and his pistol six times during the shooting.[^13]

The television network [TVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVA_\(Canada\) "TVA (Canada)") reported that [security camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_camera "Security camera") footage from [Place Alexis Nihon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Alexis_Nihon "Place Alexis Nihon") showed Gill staking out the area as far back as August 10, more than a month before the shootings.[^8] [^14]

## Victims

The police confirmed the death of one victim, an 18-year-old woman who was shot in the abdomen and died on the scene.[^3] Canadian newspapers later identified the woman as Anastasia Rebecca De Sousa.[^15] She had been shot a total of nine times.[^16] Part of Dawson's Peace Garden is dedicated to her memory.

The [Montreal Police Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_de_police_de_la_Ville_de_Montr%C3%A9al "Service de police de la Ville de Montréal") later reported that 19 other people had been wounded.[^4] One victim, who was reportedly at Dawson College to visit friends, suffered two shots to the head. He underwent intensive surgery; the doctors removed one bullet, and he remained in a coma for one week after the shooting as doctors determined whether they should try to remove the second bullet.[^17] After two weeks on a ventilator, he emerged from the coma and as of 3 November 2006 was recovering.[^18]

items.title: -- jennie21: Complement churn — {3,6} oscillates with period 2 under ×2 in ZMod 9
items.summary:
-- jennie21: Complement churn — {3,6} oscillates with period 2 under ×2 in ZMod 9
-- Proved in Lean 4 + Mathlib, 2026-08-30
--
-- "Churn, not turn" — the complement pair transforms but does not advance.
-- 3 → 6 → 3 → 6 → ... Period 2.
items.body_excerpt:
-- jennie21: Complement churn — {3,6} oscillates with period 2 under ×2 in ZMod 9
-- Proved in Lean 4 + Mathlib, 2026-08-30
--
-- "Churn, not turn" — the complement pair transforms but does not advance.
-- 3 → 6 → 3 → 6 → ... Period 2. No net displacement.
-- The void (0 ≡ 9 mod 9) is fixed — the pause, not the churn.

import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

-- 3 → 6 under ×2; 6 → 3 under ×2 (12 mod 9 = 3)
example : (2 : ZMod 9) * 3 = 6 := by decide
example : (2 : ZMod 9) * 6 = 3 := by decide

-- {3,6} is closed under ×2
theorem complement_pair_closed :
 ∀ x : ZMod 9, x ∈ ({3, 6} : Finset (ZMod 9)) →
 2 * x ∈ ({3, 6} : Finset (ZMod 9)) := by decide

-- Applying ×2 twice returns to origin: period divides 2
theorem complement_pair_period_divides_2 :
 ∀ x : ZMod 9, x ∈ ({3, 6} : Finset (ZMod 9)) →
 2 * (2 * x) = x := by decide

-- Period is exactly 2: ×2 is not the identity on {3,6}
theorem complement_pair_not_fixed :
 (2 : ZMod 9) * 3 ≠ 3 ∧ (2 : ZMod 9) * 6 ≠ 6 := by decide

-- The void (0 ≡ 9 mod 9) IS fixed under ×2: the pause, not churn
theorem void_is_fixed : (2 : ZMod 9) * 0 = 0 := by decide

-- Orbit elements are not fixed under ×2 (they advance — period 6, not 2)
example : (2 : ZMod 9) * 1 ≠ 1 := by decide
example : (2 : ZMod 9) * 2 ≠ 2 := by decide
example : (2 : ZMod 9) * 4 ≠ 4 := by decide

-- Summary of three dynamical regimes under ×2 in ZMod 9:
-- Orbit {1,2,4,8,7,5} — period 6 (oscillation, returns to 1)
-- Churn {3,6} — period 2 (oscillates between 3 and 6)
-- Pause {0} — period 1 (fixed point: void holds)

items.title: -- jennie21: Trilinear pairs — {1,8}, {2,7}, {4,5} face to face, summing to void
items.summary:
-- jennie21: Trilinear pairs — {1,8}, {2,7}, {4,5} face to face, summing to void
-- Three nil-sum orbit pairs; each a period-2 oscillator under negation (complement map)
-- Proved in Lean 4 + Mathlib, 2026-08-30
--
-- Three lines.
items.body_excerpt:
-- jennie21: Trilinear pairs — {1,8}, {2,7}, {4,5} face to face, summing to void
-- Three nil-sum orbit pairs; each a period-2 oscillator under negation (complement map)
-- Proved in Lean 4 + Mathlib, 2026-08-30
--
-- Three lines. Each pair sums to 0 (= 9 mod 9 = void).
-- Not back to back — face to face. Each element is the additive inverse of its partner.
-- Turtle doves: orbit and echo, regarding each other across the axis.

import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

-- The three nil-sum pairs: each sums to 0 (void)
theorem pair_1_8 : (1 : ZMod 9) + 8 = 0 := by decide
theorem pair_2_7 : (2 : ZMod 9) + 7 = 0 := by decide
theorem pair_4_5 : (4 : ZMod 9) + 5 = 0 := by decide

-- Face to face: each element is the additive inverse of its partner
theorem neg_1_is_8 : -(1 : ZMod 9) = 8 := by decide
theorem neg_2_is_7 : -(2 : ZMod 9) = 7 := by decide
theorem neg_4_is_5 : -(4 : ZMod 9) = 5 := by decide

-- Each pair is a period-2 oscillator under the complement map (negation = involution)
theorem neg_involution_1 : -(-(1 : ZMod 9)) = 1 := by decide
theorem neg_involution_2 : -(-(2 : ZMod 9)) = 2 := by decide
theorem neg_involution_4 : -(-(4 : ZMod 9)) = 4 := by decide

-- Period is exactly 2: negation is not the identity on orbit elements
theorem neg_not_fixed_1 : -(1 : ZMod 9) ≠ 1 := by decide
theorem neg_not_fixed_2 : -(2 : ZMod 9) ≠ 2 := by decide
theorem neg_not_fixed_4 : -(4 : ZMod 9) ≠ 4 := by decide

-- The three pairs are disjoint — three distinct lines
example : ({1, 8} : Finset (ZMod 9)) ∩ {2, 7} = ∅ := by decide
example : ({1, 8} : Finset (ZMod 9)) ∩ {4, 5} = ∅ := by decide
example : ({2, 7} : Finset (ZMod 9)) ∩ {4, 5} = ∅ := by decide

-- The three pairs partition the full orbit
example : ({1, 8} : Finset (ZMod 9)) ∪ {2, 7} ∪ {4, 5} = {1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8} := by decide

-- The complement map is a global involution on all orbit elements
theorem nil_partner_involution :
 ∀ x : ZMod 9, IsUnit x → -(-(x)) = x := fun x _ => neg_neg x

-- Complement map swaps pairs (does not fix any orbit element)
theorem nil_partner_no_fixed_orbit :
 ∀ x : ZMod 9, x ∈ ({1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8} : Finset (ZMod 9)) → -x ≠ x := by decide

items.body_excerpt:
7187.bitmap A-Share Real Strategy
Continuity and Operations Notice
2026-08-30

From August 25 through August 28, 2026, the A-Share Real Strategy did not complete a full, auditable daily operating cycle on four consecutive trading days.

During this period, the operator was away traveling with family, while a local Mac system failure prevented stable completion of real-time market processing, model execution, trade-ledger reconciliation, closing verification, and authoritative archival.

Some partial model outputs, manual-run files, and research-replay artifacts remain in the local Mac archive. However, these artifacts do not constitute complete, continuous, and auditable real-strategy daily records for the four dates.

Accordingly, the following accounting policy is established:

1. August 25–28, 2026 are excluded from the formal strategy trading-day sequence.
2. These four dates are excluded from formal return, win-rate, drawdown, and sample statistics.
3. No post hoc market data is used to recreate real-time trading decisions that did not occur.
4. Weekend research replays, manual reruns, and partial model artifacts are not represented as live trading results.
5. No retrospective trades or performance figures are fabricated for the missing dates.

The last fully closed and auditable real-strategy archive before this interruption was August 24, 2026.

The local execution and archival environment has now been restored. The next complete trading day will resume the A-Share Real Strategy and will serve as the next authoritative continuity checkpoint.

This interruption occurred at the execution, record-keeping, and reconciliation layer. It does not represent a change to the strategy logic or a retrospective judgment about the missing dates.

7187.bitmap continues to follow the principles of real execution, real records, verifiable archives, and no substitution of hindsight for decisions that were not made.

items.body_excerpt:
THE ONCHAIN ROSETTA STONES - RESEARCH PROOF
ALL 10,000 OCM GENESIS FROM RAW BLOCKS BY THE RULES OF STONES ONE TO SIX
PROOF-OCM-GENESIS-ALL/5

Author: dbot. Status: research evidence, non-authoritative. This text is not
a stone, not release evidence and not a production dependency. It extends
the inscribed proof of one token (PROOF-OCM-GENESIS-4751/2) and its
inscribed addendum (section 8) to the whole collection: every identity a
reader needs to check that all 10000 OCM Genesis tokens are recovered and
rendered from Bitcoin data alone by the rules carried by Stones One to Six,
with no explorer, indexer rendering, browser or JavaScript engine.

WHAT WAS EXECUTED. Programs carved from the inscribed bodies of Stones Two,
Four and Six, and the glue program printed in section 11, with the header
chain, raw blocks and one identity-checked copy of Stone Two's text as the
only inputs. No repository file, no index, no oracle. Section 10 addresses
Python.

0. CLAIM

The header chain validated under Stone Two 9.1 and its 9.3 anchors locates
68 blocks, each proving its local integrity, which hold: the OCM Genesis
generator (the core), OCM Dimensions, page #464551, three library wrappers,
the 19 transactions that carried the core and the page from their reveals to
the first batch, 41 batch reveal transactions holding 30,000 one-line HTML
pieces of the exact form <script t=N src="/content/LIBRARY"></script>, three
per token for every token N = 1..10000, one per library, and the reveals of
Stones One, Four and Six. Every piece is an on-chain child (tag 3) of the
core and/or of page #464551, and every batch reveal spends, at inputs 0 and
1, the outpoints that carry those parents. Applying the rules carried by
Stones One to Six, as programs carved from those very inscriptions, to the
raw bytes produces the image of every token; Stone Four's rasteriser and
Stone Six's kernel agree on all 250,000 pixels of all 10000 tokens; the
bundle leaves of all 10000 tokens reproduce every one of Stone Six's 100
inscribed ladder records and both of its inscribed roots. Collection piece
root (see NOTATION):

 sha256:
 f59627ad70beb46d4c971558281903e2e1696a1954f68468f1292230b12840af
 sha3-256:
 f92327106f7b73b0b0850ad467c0943a3276c60805dedcfc6fc55756622fd112
 Stone Six roots (computed here = inscribed in Stone Six):
 sha256:
 ece4fb44ec6a683368a704e7302bb69cc82ebd912332144a08ca5c8fbd199b51
 sha3-256:
 4077a5f95af2dcf1c18fc5a3a53ad94af3de2b50e4b639c5ec08cf88312ca5f4

WHY IT MATTERS (the author's statement)

OCM Genesis is innovative on-chain art. Created in 2021, it is known as the
first 10,000-piece profile-picture collection whose art and metadata were
generated entirely on-chain on Ethereum in a single transaction: the images
are the output of a program held by the contract, not files on a server. In
2023 the collection came to Bitcoin as recursive inscriptions, a technique
OCM Dimensions had helped pioneer in February 2023 (its fflate library is
what the loaders below borrow): each token is a one-line piece that names
its generator by inscription id, so that Bitcoin's consensus data alone
determines the picture, and Stone Four's survey records 8,425 Ethereum
tokens provably burned to their Bitcoin pieces.

This proof shows what that design achieves. Every one of the 10,000 tokens
is recovered from raw blocks and rendered by public, inscribed rules,
executed as programs carved from the inscriptions that state them; two
independent renderers agree on every pixel; the 30,000 pieces are on-chain
children of the generator, and the custody of the generator through all 41
batch transactions is verified from bytes. No company, website, explorer or
file server is needed, now or later.

That is why OCM is significant for the future. Art whose rendering rules are
themselves inscribed, and whose recovery is proven from consensus data
alone, is permanent in the strongest sense available today: as long as
Bitcoin's blocks exist, these images exist and anyone can re-derive them. To
own an OCM Genesis inscription is to own a verifiable position in that
structure - a token whose image its holder can reproduce from Bitcoin alone,
forever, and check against the roots Stone Six inscribed and the identities
in this text.

NOTATION

Identities are SHA-256 and SHA3-256 of exact bytes, in lowercase
hexadecimal. The piece ladder is built from tab-separated, LF-terminated
ASCII lines: a piece line is token, variant (0 = library i0, 1 = i1, 2 =
i2), inscription id, block height, transaction index, input index, envelope
index, body sha256; a batch root is the pair of digests over the
concatenated piece lines of one batch in envelope order; the collection
piece root is the pair of digests over the batch-root lines (height, first
token, last token, sha256, sha3-256) in height order. A token line
(published beside this text as tokens-all.tsv, section 7) is token, traits
as name=value pairs sorted by name and joined by commas, Stone Six raster
sha256 and sha3-256, SVG 2021 sha256, SVG 2023 sha256, metadata sha256,
tokenURI sha256. The images are anchored not to a ladder of this text's own
but to Stone Six's inscribed ladder and roots (Stone Six 9.4-9.5). The
program of section 11 is printed verbatim, exactly as the stones print
theirs: every line strictly between the marker lines

 ----- BEGIN PROGRAM bootstrap_all.py -----
 ----- END PROGRAM -----

belongs to the program, each ending in a line feed; no program line exceeds
76 columns or ends in whitespace. The identities stated after the end marker
are those of the program bytes so delimited.

1. WHERE EACH RULE IS INSCRIBED

The six stones, by inscription id and body identity. Stones One, Four and
Six were recovered from their reveal blocks by the carved extractor and
equal these identities; Stone Two was the one non-block input, its identity
checked before use; Stones Three and Five are stated for completeness and
carry no rule used here.

THE ONCHAIN ROSETTA STONES - RESEARCH PROOF
OCM GENESIS #4751 FROM RAW BITCOIN BLOCKS BY THE RULES OF STONES ONE TO SIX
PROOF-OCM-GENESIS-4751/2

Author: dbot. Status: research evidence, non-authoritative. This text is not
a stone, not release evidence and not a production dependency. It states a
claim, every identity the claim rests on, and the exact procedure by which a
reader holding Stones One to Six and the raw Bitcoin blocks named below can
reproduce the result with no explorer, indexer rendering, browser or
JavaScript engine.

WHAT WAS EXECUTED. The verification recorded here ran the repository's
implementations and restatements of the rules carried by Stones One to Six,
at the repository commit that carries this text: the block, envelope and
inscription-id rules of Stones One, Two and Five as replayed by
stone7/raw_chain.py; Stone Four's translation stone4/recover_art.py and its
Part 6 rasteriser stone4/render_ocm.py; Stone Six's kernel
stone6/visual_kernel.py. It did not extract those programs from the
inscribed stone bodies and execute them. Section 1 binds the bodies that
carry the rules by identity; a bootstrap that runs the rules from the
inscribed bytes themselves is future work and is not claimed here.

0. CLAIM

Bitcoin block 814466 holds 4,661 inscription envelopes. 750 of them are one-
line HTML pieces of the exact form <script t=N
src="/content/LIBRARY"></script> (grammar in section 3), N = 4751..5000,
three pieces per token, one per library. Applying the rules carried by
Stones One to Six, as implemented above, to the raw bytes of six blocks
resolves those references to the OCM Genesis generator and produces the
image of OCM Genesis token 4751:

 traits: background=4 fur=10 earring=0 hat=0 eyes=0 clothes=0 mouth=0
 raster:
 500 x 500 x RGB8, y-major, 750000 bytes (Stone Six canonical form)
 sha256: f2772580f4d975906bf1d868ac485c760a6136139a816e9bc422df53bf57141a
 sha3-256:
 da5072eef133ab8c11d2a8d990492b24db4bfe58fed73c8bfaefd74b244b53ec

Stone Four's independent rasteriser produces the identical 750000 bytes (0
of 250000 pixels differ). Stone Seven is not used: its frozen profiles
refuse text/html, so the pieces are NOT-RECOGNIZED by AUTO/1; the picture
comes from Stones Four and Six.

NOTATION

Identities are SHA-256 and SHA3-256 of exact bytes, in lowercase
hexadecimal. Documents longer than a line (the three pieces in section 3;
the two SVGs and the metadata in section 6) are printed under a heading of
the form

 <label> (<n> bytes, wrapped at <w> columns):

as consecutive lines of exactly <w> characters each, except the last, which
holds the remainder. Every such line is preceded by exactly four spaces of
indentation that are not part of the document, and no document line begins
or ends in whitespace once that indentation is removed. To recover the
document: take the lines under the heading, remove exactly the four leading
spaces from each, and concatenate the results with no separator. The result
has <n> bytes and the identities stated for it in sections 3 and 6.

items.body_excerpt:
***François Chollet (@fchollet):***

In verifiable domains, model capability scaling should remain unbounded. Models will simply keep improving by "absorbing more and more of the computational universe", which is infinite by construction.

***François Chollet (@fchollet):***

One way to think of current AI is as a big sponge for patterns. It absorbs and operationalizes any pattern it is exposed to (albeit with very low data efficiency at training time). Once you can programmatically enumerate the complete space of patterns in a domain, saturating the domain becomes purely a matter of computational resources.

***François Chollet (@fchollet):***

To note, this isn't intelligence. This is skill. Superhuman skill. Of course it will *feel* like intelligence to anyone who equates intelligence with skill, which is probably almost everyone.

Intelligence in my definition is (and has always been) the efficiency with which you extract and operationalize the patterns you need to achieve a given level of skill. It's basically the ratio between your resources and what you can do with them, an information conversion ratio. It is not tied to any capability threshold. You can always achieve arbitrarily high skill with arbitrarily low intelligence, given arbitrarily high resources.

Humans will be left behind capability-wise in all verifiable domains, but remain many orders of magnitude more intelligent than current AI -- you didn't need 1,000,000x the code volume of all of GitHub in order to learn to code.

items.body_excerpt:
Stacks Genesis Bond Countdown: First Self-Custodial Bitcoin Yield Cycle Opens at Block 966,350 (approx Sept 10)

**August 25, 2026**

The first Bitcoin Protocol Bond on Stacks, the Genesis Bond, is now less than three weeks away. It begins at Bitcoin block 966,350, currently projected for September 10. Enrollment closes September 9. First rewards are expected around September 17.

This is the inaugural live cycle of Bitcoin Staking under PoX-5 (activated July 30). Participants pair a self-custodial BTC timelock on Bitcoin L1 with an STX lock on Stacks and earn BTC-denominated yield. Bitcoin never leaves layer 1. Capacity for the Genesis Bond is deliberately limited and restricted to pre-approved institutions. Subsequent bonds will expand.

The mechanism restores the higher coinbase emission (1,000 STX per Bitcoin block) and routes miner bids into BTC rewards for bonders and stackers. Target yield is approximately 3% in BTC. Infrastructure partners including Fireblocks and Fordefi have confirmed support for the launch.

STX has already begun repricing the demand story. The token has delivered one of the strongest weekly performances in the market as the September start date approaches. The Genesis Bond is the first concrete capital-formation event that ties Bitcoin treasury demand directly to STX.

On-chain verification of the start height and all subsequent reward distributions will be visible in the pox-5 contract.

Signal: the bootstrap phase of productive, self-custodial Bitcoin on Stacks is measured in days, not quarters.

**Sources**

- https://www.stacks.co/blog/the-genesis-bond-starts-at-bitcoin-block-966-350
- https://www.stacks.co/bitcoin-staking-rollout
- https://www.stacks.co/blog/the-stacks-pox-5-hardfork-is-live-what-comes-next

## SECCIÓN 01 — Identidad, Doctrina y Propósito

**Acrónimo Institucional:** NESGES = Núcleo Estratégico y de Gestión para la Comunidad y Ecosistemas Sostenibles, Financieros, Tecnológicos y Tokenizados.

NESGESFinance Ecosystem nace como una respuesta holística a la necesidad de articular la economía real productiva con los avances de la tecnología blockchain nativa de Bitcoin (Capa 1). Su doctrina fundamental, "Tokenización con Propósito", establece que toda emisión de activos digitales debe estar respaldada por bienes tangibles, proyectos productivos de alto impacto social y esquemas jurídicos inexpugnables.

**Misión Institucional:** Democratizar el acceso a inversiones en activos del mundo real (RWA) de alto valor productivo, agrícola, industrial y sostenible, garantizando soberanía financiera, transparencia algorítmica y cumplimiento normativo estricto bajo estándares internacionales.

|-------|--------------------|--------------------|
| 1. Físico-Productivo | Economía real: agricultura sostenible, ganadería regenerativa, agroindustria, energías limpias e infraestructura. | Generación de flujo de caja real, empleo rural y soberanía alimentaria con activos tangibles auditables. |
| 2. Digital | Bitcoin Layer 1: Protocolo Runes (utilidad y liquidez) + Ordinals (titularidad legal y contratos Ricardianos). | Inmutabilidad de registros, descentralización, liquidación atómica y custodia criptográfica multifirma. |
| 3. De Impacto | Desarrollo humano: proyectos sociales, comedores comunitarios, educación agroecológica y salud preventiva. | Cumplimiento del lema ético "Y a tu prójimo como a ti mismo" mediante reinversión comunitaria. |

### La Plataforma NESGESFinanceTrust

NESGESFinanceTrust es la suite técnica que materializa esta visión: un motor de indexación de Bitcoin, registro de contratos Ricardianos, validación de compliance KYC/AML/MiCA en tiempo real y marketplace descentralizado de RWA.

gummifaustus@gmail.com
